title: Appending a tuple to a Koszul-regular prefix
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r,s\geq0$, and $a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_s\in A$. Put $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, and let $\bar b_j$ be the image of $b_j$ in $A/I$. Assume $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ is Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Then the concatenation $a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_s$ is Koszul-regular in $A$ if and only if $\bar b_1,\ldots,\bar b_s$ is Koszul-regular in $A/I$. Both empty tuples and the zero ring are allowed; no proper-ideal or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0669 (lemma-join-koszul-regular-sequences) and 068M (lemma-truncate-koszul-regular); the joining and final truncation in the proof of Tag 07CZ (lemma-koszul-independence-presentation).

proof.text: Put $B=A/I$, $P=K_\bullet(A,a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, $Q=K_\bullet(A,b_1,\ldots,b_s)$ and $C=K_\bullet(A,a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_s)$. The augmentation $\epsilon:P\to B[0]$ is reduction modulo $I$ in degree zero and zero in positive degrees. It is a chain map since $d_1(e_i)=a_i\in I$. Since $d_0=0$ and $\operatorname{im}d_1=I$, it induces $H_0(P)=A/I\xrightarrow{1}B$. All positive homology of $P$ vanishes by the assumed Koszul regularity, and negative terms are zero. Thus $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0669 (lemma-join-koszul-regular-sequences), proof, first sentence; 068M (lemma-truncate-koszul-regular), proof, first paragraph; low-degree formula from Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex).

proof.text: The finite direct-sum total complex $\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_A P)$ has differential $d(y\otimes x)=d_Qy\otimes x+(-1)^q y\otimes d_Px$ on $Q_q\otimes P_p$. Define $\theta:\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_A P)\to C$ by $y_J\otimes x_I\mapsto y_J\wedge x_I$, where $x_I$ and $y_J$ are the increasing standard wedges in the prefix and tail blocks of $A^{r+s}$. Every increasing wedge in the combined basis splits uniquely into those two blocks, and $y_J\wedge x_I=(-1)^{pq}x_I\wedge y_J$, so this gives an invertible map in every degree. The explicit Koszul differential satisfies $d(y_J\wedge x_I)=d_Qy_J\wedge x_I+(-1)^q y_J\wedge d_Px_I$: deleting a prefix basis vector crosses exactly the $q$ tail vectors. Hence $\theta$ is a chain isomorphism. This is the joining identification with the tensor factors in the reverse order.

source.place: Tag 0664 (lemma-join-sequences-koszul-complex), statement and proof hint; the basis bijection and differential check expand the omitted proof using Tag 0623.

proof.text: Reindex every chain complex as a cochain complex by $L^i=L_{-i}$; tensor degrees and signs agree because $(-1)^{-q}=(-1)^q$. The terms of $Q$ are finite free and $Q^i=0$ outside $[-s,0]$. They are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $Q$ K-flat as an ordinary $A$-module complex [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Apply clause (ii) of [lem-pc-mixed-tensor-kflat-quasi-iso] with both coefficient rings equal to $A$, ring map the identity, $F=Q$, and $u=\epsilon:P\to B[0]$. It gives a quasi-isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(1_Q\otimes\epsilon):\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_A P)\to Q\otimes_A B$. In particular this does not require $B$ to be flat or K-flat over $A$. Together with $\theta$ it compares $C$ with $Q\otimes_A B$ by a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0669 and 068M, proof, total-tensor comparison; supporting Tag 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism) and Tag 06Y0 (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism), applied in the symmetric tensor order.

proof.text: Write $\bar Q=K_\bullet(B,\bar b_1,\ldots,\bar b_s)$. The map $Q_n\otimes_A B\to\bar Q_n$, $y_J\otimes\bar c\mapsto\bar c\,\bar y_J$, is invertible: both modules are free over $B$ on the same increasing subsets $J$ of size $n$, with inverse $\bar y_J\mapsto y_J\otimes1$. The differential formula in [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] reduces coefficient $b_j$ to $\bar b_j$, so these maps form a chain isomorphism. For a complex of $B$-modules, forgetting to $A$-modules changes neither the sets of cycles nor boundaries, and therefore changes neither whether its homology is zero. The quasi-isomorphism in step 3 and the isomorphism in step 2 show that $H_n(C)=0$ for all $n>0$ if and only if $H_n(\bar Q)=0$ for all $n>0$. Both complexes have zero negative terms. By [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], these are exactly the two asserted Koszul-regularity conditions.

source.place: Tags 0669 and 068M, proof, identification with the quotient-ring Koszul complex and conclusion.

proof.text: All constructions include the empty subset as the degree-zero basis. If $r=0$, $I=0$, $P=A[0]$ and $\epsilon$ is the identity. If $s=0$, $Q=A[0]$ and the conclusion compares the assumed regularity of the prefix with the automatic regularity of the empty tuple over $B$. If $A=0$ or $I=A$, the corresponding quotient complexes have zero terms; the same quasi-isomorphism still applies. Thus no properness of $I$, positive length, or Noetherian hypothesis was introduced.
